newsitem.title: UK: CIPS says UK services growth picks up in March.
newsitem.headline: CIPS says UK services growth picks up in March.

text.p: Activity in Britain's services sector picked up pace in March with output, new and outstanding business, employment and prices all rising, the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply (CIPS) said on Thursday. CIPS said the seasonally adjusted business activity index, which measures output of the service economy, has recorded an expansion of activity every month since last July when the survey began, with growth accelerating sharply in March.
The index stood at a seasonally adjusted 63.3 compared with 60.4 in February and 56.6 last July.

Indices are calculated to measure changes in business conditions, with readings above 50 indicating an expansion and below 50 a contraction. The greater the divergence from 50.0 the greater the rate of change indicated.
The survey is based on responses from a panel of 500 UK business executives in private sector service industries, excluding wholesale and retail.
"Over 35 percent of all companies reported an increase in business activity while just 9.0 percent reported a decline," CIPS said.
March also saw the largest increase in new business since the survey began. The incoming new business index rose to 62.4 percent from 60.9 in February and 57.1 percent last July.

"The growth in demand over the past nine months has generally been attributed simply to the improved economic climate, which a growing number of firms have taken advantage of through greater sales and marketing activity," CIPS said.
It said a consequence of this growth of incoming new business has been a rise in the amount of work outstanding, or work in hand, which also rose sharply, to 57.7 in March from 54.6 in February.

But the survey found a growing number of firms have been unable to meet demand due to lack of resources -- most notably a lack of highly skilled personel. The input cost index rose to 57.0 from 56.9 in February, indicating a further rise in input prices. CIPS said the major input cost is labour and reflects higher wages being paid in the sector.
"With the labour market continuing to tighten, rising wages and salaries were found to have been the principal cause of a further increase in costs during March," it said.
But it found that robust demand allowed firms to pass these higher costs on in the form of higher prices.
Price charged rose for the fifth month in a row with the average prices index reaching 51.6. But that compares with 51.8 in February, showing the rate of price rises is easing.
"Only 10 percent of firms were able to raise prices (in March)," CIPS said.

Looking ahead, three quarters of all companies said they expected higher activity in a year's time and only 6.0 percent forsaw a decline. "Such buoyant confidence has been evident for nine months running," the survey said.
(All seasonally adjusted) MARCH FEBRUARY JULY 96
Business activity index 63.3 60.4 56.6
Incoming new business 62.4 60.9 57.1
Outstanding business 57.7 54.6 52.3
Employment 57.6 56.8 54.4
Average prices charged 51.6 51.8 47.8
Average input prices 57.0 56.9 52.7
Business expectations 84.6 85.8 82.1
